miniProject.title: General multi-head block with an intervention battery
miniProject.brief: Implement a pre-norm transformer block with multi-head attention, masks and positions from tensor operations, derive its cost for a stated shape, and prove with interventions that future and padded tokens cannot change valid causal outputs.
steps: Implement scaled dot-product attention with a stable softmax and boolean causal and padding masks. Pass Deep-ML 490 and the CS231n Assignment 3 MultiHeadAttention and PositionalEncoding checks in Transformer_Captioning.ipynb.
Build multi-head attention with an explicit split, transpose and merge, self- and cross-attention through one module, and valid lengths repeated per head in batch-major order.

Assemble a pre-norm block (norm, attention, add, norm, gated MLP, add) with sinusoidal or learned positions. Check shapes across depths, batch sizes and sequence lengths, and identical eval-mode outputs after saving and reloading the state_dict.

Run the intervention battery on the composed block: changing future tokens leaves earlier outputs unchanged, changing padded content leaves valid outputs unchanged, and permuting the batch permutes the outputs. Show that sequence permutation passes without mask or positions and fails with the causal mask.

Differential-test forward and backward against torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention on the math backend, within tolerance, with noncontiguous inputs and variable lengths, excluding fully masked rows. Pin your fully-masked-row convention in a separate test.
Derive parameters, forward FLOPs and score memory for n = 512, d = 1024, h = 16 in fp32, then measure the score tensor bytes and a profiler FLOP count and reconcile them under stated conventions.
deliverables: The attention and block package with masks, positions and the gated MLP.
The test suite: oracle checks, the intervention battery, the SDPA differential tests and the fully-masked-row convention test.
A cost sheet for the stated shape with measured numbers beside derived ones.

checks.name: CS231n Assignment 3, Transformer_Captioning.ipynb attention and positional-encoding checks
checks.note: Run the notebook cells locally; each prints a rel_error against stored values or numerical gradients. Gradescope is for enrolled students only, so these printed checks are the gate.

rubric.pass: Deep-ML 490 and the CS231n attention checks pass.
rubric.strong: Forward and backward match the SDPA math backend in float64 on noncontiguous inputs.

rubric.pass: Future-token and padding interventions leave valid outputs unchanged.
rubric.strong: The battery passes on shapes you did not tune for, and the causal sequence-permutation test fails as it should.

rubric.pass: Split, transpose and merge match a loop over heads.
rubric.strong: A test shows that tiling valid lengths with repeat masks the wrong heads while repeat_interleave masks the right ones.

rubric.pass: Shapes hold across depths, and eval-mode outputs survive a save and reload.
rubric.strong: You compare pre-norm and post-norm on a short training run and report gradient norms per layer.

rubric.pass: Parameters, FLOPs and score bytes are derived for the stated shape.
rubric.strong: Measured score bytes and profiler FLOPs agree with the derivation, with each convention stated, such as multiply-adds versus FLOPs and MiB versus MB.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone artifact 2 can use a model built on this block; the LLM Foundations stage builds its decoder from the same parts.
